- The padded zeros do not affect the sum but ensure the tree structure remains complete [S2, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that non-power-of-two input sizes are handled by zero-padding the input array to the next power of two. The code snippet shows `cudaMemset(dev_idata + n, 0, ...)` which fills the padded region with zeros. In the context of the stream compaction algorithm described (mapping to booleans, scanning, scattering), adding zeros to the input array results in zeros in the boolean mask (since `idata[index] == 0`). An exclusive scan on a mask of zeros produces indices that correspond to the end of the valid data range or are simply skipped during scattering (since the condition `bools[idx] == 1` will be false for the padded zeros). Therefore, the padded zeros do not contribute to the count of non-zero elements (the sum of the boolean mask) and do not appear in the output, effectively ensuring the tree structure (based on power-of-two size) remains complete without affecting the logical result.
